title: IBM OM crossbar ordinary supervised-BP post-fault recovery control
hypothesis: Starting from the same continuous-HWA healthy P0 states and the same chronological AIHWKit-compatible published corrupt-device transition used by the STAR-inspired smoke, one full 55,000-example epoch of ordinary ground-truth cross-entropy backpropagation with digital Adam and physical pulse writes will produce positive mean apparent-forward recovery, improve at least three of four programming endpoints, lose no more than two percentage points on any endpoint, and recover at least 25% of the mean fault damage. The separately declared 16-example one-step arm matches the example cohort and learning rate, but not STAR's sequential local-update mechanism, and is not a sufficient test of reparability.
motivation: The STAR-inspired 16-example technical canary did not repair the network, but its update budget issued only tens of pulses. This matched control asks whether the same post-deployment damage is compensable at all by ordinary end-to-end retraining before attributing failure to the local STAR objective. It intentionally uses labels, full cross-layer backpropagation, autograd, a W2-transpose gradient path, and digital Adam state, so it is a privileged algorithmic ceiling rather than a fully local on-chip learner.

arms.description: One ordinary cross-entropy BP/pulse-Adam step on the same deterministic 16-example budget as the local STAR smoke.
One fixed ordinary retraining epoch over all 55,000 post-split MNIST training examples, with no learning-rate tuning or checkpoint selection.

completion_criteria: Both declared configs complete exactly once and reproduce one healthy repaired IBM-OM assignment 87004, endpoint seeds 89402-89405, the 784-50-10 analog-MVM--digital-ReLU--analog-MVM architecture, the same five one-minibatch continuous-HWA predeployment path, the first 1000 official MNIST test examples, and no fresh-array transfer or checkpoint selection.

For each endpoint and arm, the saved healthy P0 and immediate faulted checkpoints are hash-bound and replayable only with the exact healthy population, published companion population, and healthy P0 authority. The two arms must have bit-exact healthy persistent/apparent states, fault masks, stuck q values, immediate faulted persistent/apparent states, and pulse baselines before retraining begins.

The published companion explicitly enables OM corrupt_devices_prob=0.1348 despite the preset default 0.0 and retains corrupt_devices_range=0.01. Every selected active state has collapsed bounds inside the AIHWKit range and zero upward/downward increments; stuck-site persistent q=a-r stays bit-exact during repair, while apparent q retains write-noise resampling on attempted writes.

The recovery update uses ground-truth labels and cross-entropy only. The update helper receives current apparent q through a restricted state/pulse port and no teacher logits or fault mask; it uses ordinary full-network autograd/backpropagation, the W2-transpose hidden error path, digital Adam betas 0.9/0.999 and epsilon 1e-8, q learning rates [6e-5,6e-5], all layers, and a 64-command per-cell cap.

The matched arm records exactly one ordered 16-example minibatch and one optimizer step. The primary arm records exactly one ordered 55,000-example epoch in 3438 minibatches. Each repair stream is hashed independently; the predeployment HWA remains restricted to the original 16-example one-minibatch stream in both arms.

Every endpoint reports healthy, immediate-fault, and fixed-final apparent-forward and persistent-q diagnostic accuracy; prediction hashes; cross-entropy and pre-update training accuracy; optimizer steps; commanded pulses and cells; commands to immutable and programmable cells; actual healthy persistent-q movement; cap hits; probability clipping; and proof that stuck-site persistent q is unchanged.

The result remains exploratory model evidence. Four endpoint streams on one assignment are not independent arrays, apparent q is a post-write state rather than a fresh inference read, and no claim of fully on-chip learning, fabricated defect rates, retention robustness, line-resistance tolerance, power, or endurance is permitted.
analysis_plan: Apply provenance and chronology gates before accuracy. If the two arms do not reproduce bit-exact healthy P0 and immediate faulted states, or if either learner sees teacher logits or the fault mask, classify the comparison invalid.

For each arm and endpoint, report healthy apparent accuracy, immediate faulted apparent accuracy, fixed-final apparent accuracy, fault damage in percentage points, recovery gain in percentage points, and recovery fraction gain/(healthy-faulted) when damage is positive. Report all four endpoints, arithmetic mean, and range.

Call the fault relevant only if mean apparent damage is at least two percentage points. Call full-epoch ordinary retraining promising only if mean gain is positive, at least three of four endpoints improve, no endpoint loses more than two points, and mean recovery fraction is at least 0.25. Call it strong only if final mean apparent accuracy is at least 90% and mean recovery fraction is at least 0.5.

Use the 16-example arm only to compare mechanism at the tiny matched budget; do not use its failure to conclude that normal retraining cannot repair. Compare it descriptively with the STAR-inspired 16-example result only after exact P0/fault parity is established.
Report persistent-q diagnostics beside apparent-forward results. Apparent improvement without persistent improvement is an endpoint-noise-sensitive repair warning, not stable physical recovery.

Separate pulse commands to immutable versus programmable cells and actual healthy persistent movement. A command sent to a stuck site is not repair of that site; any compensation must arise from programmable cells.

Do not tune the learning rate, epoch count, pulse cap, data cohort, or select a checkpoint after observing these results. If the pinned 6e-5 full epoch fails, preserve it and predeclare a separate follow-up rather than editing this study.
